beam.description: Long-context memory benchmark: 100 conversations (100K–10M tokens), 2 000 questions across 10 memory ability categories.

lifebench.description: Long-horizon multi-source personalized memory benchmark across 10 users.

locomo.description: Multi-session long-term conversations with 1,986 QA pairs.

locomo-fixed.description: LoComo without the questions its conversations cannot answer (gold answer absent from the conversation, gold contradicting it, or the question naming the wrong person).

longmemeval.description: Long-term memory evaluation in LLM-based chat assistants.

personamem.description: Long-horizon personal preference tracking across conversation sessions.

precisionmembench.description: Belief-level retrieval precision: 77 cases asserting exactly which memories must and must not surface.

sdebench.description: Does memory help a coding agent? Bug-fix tasks whose obvious fix fails a hidden test.

supportbench.description: Does a support agent use the product docs and each customer's history correctly? Real Nextcloud 32 manuals (837 PDF pages) plus per-customer support chats and approved exceptions.

vidore-v3-markdown.description: ViDoRe V3, 8 enterprise PDF tasks (EN + FR) as the page markdown the dataset ships, one text document per page; text-to-page search in 6 query languages.
vidore-v3-markdown.scoring_note: nDCG@10 (trec_eval linear gain) over every query of all 6 query languages, against ViDoRe's page-level qrels. The average split is the mean over the 8 tasks, the number Mixedbread's table reports. Search only: no LLM, no reranker, no query rewriting.

vidore-v3-pdf.description: ViDoRe V3, 8 enterprise PDF tasks as the raw source PDFs: the server reads and splits each file itself, and a hit on page n stands for that page.
vidore-v3-pdf.scoring_note: nDCG@10 (trec_eval linear gain) over every query of all 6 query languages, against ViDoRe's page-level qrels. The average split is the mean over the 8 tasks, the number Mixedbread's table reports. Search only: no LLM, no reranker, no query rewriting. Harder than the markdown version: nobody parses the pages for the server.

atm-bench-retrieval.description: ATM-Bench as search: 3,759 photos, 533 videos and 6,742 emails (four years of one person's data), 1,013 questions scored on their human-labelled evidence items.
atm-bench-retrieval.scoring_note: R@10: the share of a question's evidence items in the top 10 results. Each photo and video goes in as the raw file and as the benchmark's own text record (time, place, caption, OCR, tags); a hit on either counts as the item.

legalbench-rag.description: LegalBench-RAG mini: 776 questions over 714 contracts (NDAs, M&A agreements, commercial contracts, privacy policies), scored on the exact characters lawyers marked.
legalbench-rag.scoring_note: Character recall@5, as legalbenchrag/run_benchmark.py computes it: the share of the marked characters that the top 5 results' text covers. The 4 sets weigh the same (194 questions each). The search runs at the API's default budget of 4,096 tokens, so the 5 results carry about as much text as 5 chunks of a typical RAG setup. Precision (the share of returned text that is marked) is in each query's metrics. Documents go in with neutral names. Search only: no LLM.

atmem.description: Local auditable memory with deterministic extraction, lifecycle governance, SQLite persistence, lexical/graph retrieval, and calibrated direct-support selection.

coding-plugin.description: Hindsight coding-agents plugin: deepen-engine ingestion, agent-side reflect+inject.

local.description: Embedded Hindsight fact store using gemini-2.5-flash-lite as the extraction model. Recall uses all memory types (world + experience + observation) with no type filter applied.

cloud.description: Hindsight hosted cloud API. Recall uses all memory types (world + experience + observation) with no type filter applied.

http.description: Hindsight via a self-hosted HTTP endpoint. Recall uses all memory types (world + experience + observation) with no type filter applied.

knowledge.description: Hindsight knowledge banks over HTTP: files (PDF, image, video) and text written into a knowledge bank, then searched. No LLM: the server's knowledge embedder is the only model.

support-memory.description: supportbench arm: manuals, chats and approved exceptions all retained into one memory bank; reflect answers.

support-knowledge.description: supportbench arm: manuals, chats and approved exceptions all in one knowledge bank, linked to an empty memory bank; reflect answers.

support-linked.description: supportbench arm: chats in a memory bank, manuals and approved exceptions in a linked knowledge bank; reflect answers.

bm25.description: Keyword search baseline. No embeddings — splits docs into chunks and uses BM25 ranking.

cognee.description: Graph-based knowledge extraction with FastEmbed (BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5) + OpenAI LLM.

mastra.description: Mastra semantic recall with LibSQL store and FastEmbed embeddings. topK=10.

mastra-om.description: Mastra Observational Memory: observer/reflector pattern with Gemini 2.5 Flash + GPT-4o.

local.description: Agentic memory with Gemini 2.5 Flash for reflective extraction + local Qdrant store.

cloud.description: Mem0 cloud API. Async indexing — waits for indexing to complete before eval. k=20.

local.description: Ogham MCP: hybrid vector + BM25 search with entity overlap boost. Local Postgres + pgvector. Stores verbatim conversations and retrieves via Reciprocal Rank Fusion with optional read-time fact extraction.

hybrid-search.description: Hybrid dense + sparse vector search via Qdrant with RRF fusion. Dense: Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B (1024d, asymmetric query/doc encoding). Sparse: BM42 (bm42-all-minilm-l6-v2-attentions). Documents chunked into 512-token windows before indexing. Retrieves top-k=50 chunks (prefetch 100 per branch).

supermemory.description: Supermemory cloud API with temporal metadata support.

rag.description: Default. Provider retrieves top-k documents; they are injected into an LLM prompt as context. Supports both MCQ and open-ended questions.

agentic-rag.description: The LLM acts as an agent with a recall tool and can make multiple retrieval calls with different queries before finalising its answer.

agent.description: Bypasses the benchmark retrieval pipeline entirely — calls the provider's own native direct_answer() for providers that have built-in agentic answering.

coding.description: Build the task repo, run a coding agent with test-feedback interventions, grade by pytest.

retrieval.description: No LLM. Returns the provider's retrieved memories verbatim; the dataset scores the returned ID set.
